issue_context.title: Writable does not check if stream has been destroyed during _final and _write
issue_context.body: Not sure if this is a problem but I think we should at least add a comment in the code that this case has been considered.
comments: @nodejs/streams

I don't know to be honest as I don't want to make things too stringent. However adding a check is going to improve the developer experience.

What should the check do? Throw? emit `'error'`?

I think:

1. cancel any further substeps
2. if stream was destroyed without error, override with error
Should we tag this as good first issue?
@ronag Can i take this up?
Go for it!
Hey! I was wondering about the status of this issue, and if I could try looking into it?
Go for it!

I went through [Writable.js](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/1c4df352b77514e93a46fb27e996755d45a0b530/lib/internal/streams/writable.js), but I'm not sure where should the checks be added. Specifically, I found these to be already present:
- [_write](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/1c4df352b77514e93a46fb27e996755d45a0b530/lib/internal/streams/writable.js#L284) at [line 321](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/1c4df352b77514e93a46fb27e996755d45a0b530/lib/internal/streams/writable.js#L321) checks for `state.destroyed` before going to the user-provided `_write` function
- `_final` seems to be called through `prefinish` which also  checks for `state.destroyed` at [line 718](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/1c4df352b77514e93a46fb27e996755d45a0b530/lib/internal/streams/writable.js#L718)

I'll really appreciate some guidance on this
You need to look at the time between those being called and their callback being invoked.

Thanks! I followed the code between these two times, and wanted to confirm the location. For `_write`, will it be appropriate to  place the check inside [onwrite()](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/1b335d41a405f491a84c4d8cb51fabd4615c0306/lib/internal/streams/writable.js#L426) ?   

This will be for the case when the stream gets destroyed during `_write` but no error is passed to the callback.

After looking into this, this seems to run counter to a previous pull request (maybe I didn't understand something?): https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/24062
Of course, the project requirements might have changed since then too.

I can't immediately see a way to throw an error at the start of the callbacks without changing/removing several of the tests. I also foresee some issues with asynchronous implementations of _write and _final (also in the tests). Do we want to go ahead with the change anyway?
When I went through `Writable.js` I was unable to understand the `state.sync` flag, could anyone explain what it is?

Seems to be an interesting research topic. 
Let me know and we arrange a meeting for discussing it.
Hey i was wondering if this issue is still open and if i can take a crack at it 😸

> 
> 1. cancel any further substeps
> 2. if stream was destroyed without error, override with error
